result: CCR7 simultaneously recruits G protein and β-arrestin upon chemokine stimulation, forming a 'megaplex' complex. CCL19 promotes stronger co-recruitment than CCL21, with both ligands enabling β-arrestin translocation to endosomes in a tail conformation that permits continued G protein binding.
evaluation: All three reviewers accept the data showing simultaneous G protein and β-arrestin recruitment. Reviewer 3 states 'the authors claims supported by the data' and notes the experiments are 'well controlled and executed.' The NanoBiT and microscopy data in Figures 2 are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: Internalized CCR7 activates G protein from endosomes. CCL19 promotes robust endosomal Gi/o activation while CCL21 predominantly activates Gi/o at the cell surface with only modest endosomal signaling, as demonstrated by multiple biosensor approaches.
evaluation: Reviewers 2 and 3 explicitly affirm this finding. Reviewer 3 states the authors 'provide substantial evidence that chemokine receptors can stimulate G proteins from within endosomes' and that this 'builds upon earlier studies.' Reviewer 2 notes 'some findings verify previous studies (e.g. endomembrane signalling).' The data in Figure 3 are not challenged.

result: APEX2 proximity labeling proteomics reveals that endosomal CCR7 uniquely enriches specific Rho GTPase regulators, trafficking proteins, and signaling molecules compared to plasma membrane CCR7. A total of 584 proteins were identified with differential enrichment patterns between CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation.
evaluation: All reviewers emphasize the value of the APEX2 proteomics data. Reviewer 1 states 'The APEX2 resource will be valuable to the GPCR and immunology community' and notes it 'offers many opportunities to follow up on findings.' Reviewer 2 calls these 'the most novel findings' and states the resource 'will be valuable.' Reviewer 3 describes the approach as 'unbiased' and notes the data 'may provide clues' for other receptors.

result: Endosomal CCR7 signaling is directly associated with enhanced Rac1 activity. CCL19 promotes significantly greater Rac1 activation than CCL21, and this activation depends on receptor internalization and Gi/o signaling, as demonstrated by endocytosis inhibitors and phosphorylation site mutations.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without challenge. Reviewer 3 notes the authors 'used the resource to validate earlier findings' and that the study 'builds upon earlier studies from the Legler group which showed that endocytosed CCR7 could activate Rac1.' The data in Figure 6 linking endosomal signaling to Rac1 are not questioned.

result: Endosomal CCR7 signaling promotes chemotaxis of immune T cells. Jurkat T cells migrate more efficiently toward CCL19 than CCL21, and this migration depends on Gi/o signaling, receptor internalization, and Rac1 activity, as shown by inhibitor studies.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the chemotaxis data. Reviewer 3 states the authors 'provide substantial evidence that chemokine receptors can stimulate G proteins from within endosomes to regulate signalling pathways involved in cell migration.' The transwell migration data in Figure 7 are not challenged by any reviewer.

result: CCL19 and CCL21 differentially regulate β-arrestin recruitment and CCR7 internalization. CCL19 promotes robust β-arrestin recruitment and receptor internalization to endosomes, while CCL21 causes only partial responses. Both ligands equally inhibit cAMP production, confirming they are full agonists for Gi/o signaling.
evaluation: These characterization data are accepted by all reviewers. Reviewer 2 notes 'some findings verify previous studies' and Reviewer 3 states 'data are well presented, with the authors claims supported by the data.' The differential effects of CCL19 vs CCL21 shown in Figure 1 are foundational to the study and not questioned.

result: Background and contextual claims about GPCR signaling, chemokine receptors, CCR7 biology, Rho GTPases, and prior literature on endosomal signaling and cell migration.
evaluation: These are established knowledge claims and literature citations that provide context for the study. Reviewers do not challenge any of these background statements. Reviewer 3 notes the paper 'has an excellent narrative which makes it relatively easy to follow,' implicitly accepting the contextual framework.
